description: Public benchmark results used as pass-rate inputs. Solvency needs only pass_rate from a benchmark; cost is normally recomputed from current verified prices in models.json. Sources that publish their own measured per-task cost are marked cost_basis='measured_by_source'. Sources that publish complete measured token usage can be marked cost_basis='source_usage_repriced' and repriced at current verified model prices. Both bypass Solvency's loop model entirely.
redistribution_policy: Every row here is THIRD-PARTY data, ingested by reference. None of it may be republished in Solvency's CC-BY /data export. Rows carry redistributable=false and must be surfaced as attributed, linked citations only. Only Solvency's own Phase 3 measured runs are published as open data.

cost_bases.measured_by_source: The source ran the model and observed the cost. Uses real token usage; no Solvency loop-count assumption applies. Priced at the source's own pricing snapshot, which Solvency cannot recompute without per-model token counts.
cost_bases.source_usage_repriced: The source measured complete per-attempt token usage. Solvency divides aggregate usage by countable attempts and applies the model's current verified input, cached-input and output prices. No task-tier, loop-count, cache-hit or frontier-efficiency assumption applies.
cost_bases.modelled_by_solvency: The source publishes only a pass rate. Cost comes from Solvency's loop model (an ASSUMPTION) times current verified prices.
cost_bases.historical_at_run_date: The source published a cost, but at the prices in force on run_date. Never displayed as a current figure.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v1.4
sources.scoring: Task-normalized average pass@1: the 3 attempts are averaged per task, then task scores are averaged so every task has equal weight. All component outcomes are binary. Index is a simple average of the 3 component scores.
sources.cost_methodology: Average pay-per-token API cost per task using provider token pricing, with cached input priced separately from uncached input and cache-write charges included where providers bill for them. Not consumer plan pricing.
sources.verified_via: live page read in-browser; the leaderboard table is client-rendered and is not visible to plain HTTP fetch
sources.attribution_note: Exact string and hyperlink required by the Data Platform Terms, section 5. Do not paraphrase.
caveats: Rows are HARNESS + MODEL combinations, not bare models. Claude Code + Opus 5 is not the same measurement as Opus 5 in another harness; AA's own harness comparison shows the harness materially changes the score. Never present an AA figure as a property of the model alone.

Index scores are read from the published chart as 0-100 composite values. Solvency derives pass_rate = index / 100 on the basis that the index is an average of task-normalized pass@1 rates. This derivation is an INTERPRETATION, flagged per row as pass_rate_derivation.

Per-model token counts are published as charts only; numeric values were not captured, so Solvency cannot recompute AA's cost at current prices. AA's cost is carried as measured, at AA's pricing snapshot.
AA notes prompt cache hit rates vary significantly by provider routing, which can materially change effective cost.
sources.newest_entry_note: Index v1.4 read live on this date; AA does not stamp a per-row run date.

sources.name: OpenBench GPT-5.6 Sol harness comparison
sources.scoring: Binary deterministic checkers over 15 admission-gated tasks, three trials per harness. Solve rate is solved/countable attempts; infrastructure and rate-limited failures are excluded under the source methodology.
measures: proxy-measured uncached input, cache-read and output tokens
sources.cost_methodology: Solvency averages OpenBench's proxy-measured token totals over each arm's countable attempts, then applies GPT-5.6 Sol prices verified 2026-08-21: $5/M uncached input, $0.50/M cached input and $30/M output. OpenBench did not publish a metered dollar bill, so this is source usage repriced by Solvency, not measured_by_source.
sources.verified_via: Re-derived from the digest-sealed published results.jsonl and provenance.json at OpenBench commit db193457a3d9128cd4d01fd839c2a890c186c9ac.
caveats: This source is isolated from Solvency's general model leaderboard. Its 15-task, three-trial harness arms must never be ranked against AA's 326-task model rows or any other benchmark bundle.

Only Pi, Claude Code, Grok Build and Codex are ingested: every countable cell in those arms has complete proxy-measured input/cache/output usage. Cursor and OpenCode use CLI-self-reported tokens; Devin lacks complete split usage.
Correctness intervals are wide at 44-45 countable attempts per arm. Mid-table point-estimate differences must not be described as statistically decisive.
The source notes Pi was being rerun to investigate a surprising per-task swing; recheck the sealed release before using this as a long-lived headline.
sources.newest_entry_note: Release date. The sealed result rows were generated across the preceding run window.

sources.name: Scale SEAL leaderboard - SWE-bench Pro (public)
sources.scoring: Pass@1, every model run through the same scaffolding (SWE-Agent standard; rows marked * use the mini-swe-agent harness). Turn limit 250 standard, 50 for cost-capped rows.
sources.attribution: Source: Scale SEAL leaderboard, SWE-bench Pro
caveats: Per-model dollar cost was NOT captured from the page. These rows therefore use Solvency's loop model for cost, which is an assumption. Marked cost_basis='modelled_by_solvency'.
Only a partial leaderboard was captured (6 rows visible). This is not the complete SEAL table.
Last-updated date is not stated on the page, so staleness cannot be computed for this source.

sources_evaluated_and_rejected.name: Holistic Agent Leaderboard (HAL), Princeton SAgE
sources_evaluated_and_rejected.why_rejected: Publishes standardized agent runs with centralized cost tracking across 9 benchmarks and 26,597 rollouts, which is exactly the right shape. But the project states it has PAUSED updating with new models to focus on reliability measurement, and its most recent entries date to August-September 2025. It covers GPT-5, o3, o4-mini and Claude Opus/Sonnet of that era, not the 2026 generation. Same staleness failure as Aider, from a different direction.
sources_evaluated_and_rejected.newest_entry_note: Source describes its most recent entries as August-September 2025; midpoint used and flagged approximate.
